summary: ```# Introduction to New Features of Marvelous Designer 11: Process from Marvelous Designer to Maya ## Overview This document outlines the steps to create costume animations using the animation character in M.I.E. (Marvelous Designer Integration Environment) and how to export these animations for use in Maya. ## Preparing the Animation Character 1. **Prepare the Joint Key Needle**: Begin by preparing the joint key needle in M.I.E. 2. **Select the Body Grid**: Choose the body grid for the Alambic file. While Alambic is the focus of this tutorial, other formats such as FBX and PC2 can also be used. ## Saving the Animation File - After selecting the appropriate body, save the animation file. ## Importing into Marvelous Designer 1. **Open the Costume File**: Launch Marvelous Designer and open the costume file you wish to work with. 2. **Import the Alambic File**: Import the Alambic file that you previously saved from M.I.E. ## Adjusting the Model Surface - **Surface Diameter**: Adjust the surface of the model. The surface diameter determines the distance between the body grid and the costume during the simulation process. Since the character used in this video is much smaller than a normal adult, reduce the surface diameter to the default setting. ## Simulation Process - **Activate Simulation**: Activate the simulation or press the control key to verify if the costume is properly worn on the body. - **Recording the Animation**: After pausing the simulation, click the record button to initiate the animation operation and record the animation simultaneously. ## Exporting the Costume Animation 1. **Exporting to M.I.E.**: Once the animation is complete, export the costume with the animation back to M.I.E. 2. **Export File Type**: The costume animation will be exported to an Alambic file, which is the most commonly used file type. Other formats such as PCO and MC can also be utilized if needed. ### Merging Connection Points - If you need to merge the connection points, select the merge option. Additionally, select the unified UV coordinates to export the UV created in Marvelous Designer. ### Pattern Preparation - If preparing the pattern is unnecessary, you can cancel it in the subsequent options box. ## Finalizing Export Settings - **Unit Selection**: Choose 0mm as the unit in the ratio, as it aligns with the unit used during exportation. - **Confirmation**: Select the confirm button to finalize your settings. ## Importing Costume File to M.I.E. 1. **Import Process**: Now, import the costume file back to M.I.E. 2. **Cache Saving**: Press cache to save. You may also select Alambic to save the cache. 3. **Select Costume File**: Navigate to Alambic, find, and select the costume file. ## Conclusion With these steps, you can start working on animated costumes within M.I.E. and enhance your projects using Marvelous Designer and Maya. ```
